const OPTIMIZED_DEPENDENCY_MAP_PATH_PREFIX = '/node_modules/.vite/deps/'
const JAVASCRIPT_MAP_EXTENSION = '.js.map'
const LINE_SOURCE_MAP_DIRECTIVE_PATTERN = /^\s*\/\/[#@]\s*sourceMappingURL=.*$/gmu
const BLOCK_SOURCE_MAP_DIRECTIVE_PATTERN = /\/\*[#@]\s*sourceMappingURL=.*?\*\//gsu
const JSON_CONTENT_TYPE = 'application/json'
const LOCAL_URL_BASE = 'http://localhost'

const TEST_WORKERS = 2

type NextFunction = (error?: Error) => void

type SourceMapWithSourcesContent = {
    sourcesContent?: unknown
    [key: string]: unknown
}

function requestPathFromUrl(url: string | undefined) {
    if (!url) return null

    return new URL(url, LOCAL_URL_BASE).pathname
}

function isOptimizedDependencyMapRequest(requestPath: string) {
    return requestPath.startsWith(OPTIMIZED_DEPENDENCY_MAP_PATH_PREFIX) && requestPath.endsWith(JAVASCRIPT_MAP_EXTENSION)
}

function isInsideDirectory(filePath: string, directoryPath: string) {
    return filePath.toLowerCase().startsWith(`${directoryPath.toLowerCase()}${sep}`)
}

function resolveOptimizedDependencyMapPath(server: ViteDevServer, requestPath: string) {
    const relativePath = decodeURIComponent(requestPath.slice(1))
    const mapPath = resolve(server.config.root, relativePath)
    const optimizedDependencyDirectory = resolve(server.config.root, 'node_modules', '.vite', 'deps')

    if (!isInsideDirectory(mapPath, optimizedDependencyDirectory)) throw new Error(`Invalid optimized dependency map path: ${requestPath}`)

    return mapPath
}

function stripNestedSourceMapDirectives(source: string) {
    return source
        .replace(LINE_SOURCE_MAP_DIRECTIVE_PATTERN, '')
        .replace(BLOCK_SOURCE_MAP_DIRECTIVE_PATTERN, '')
}

export function sanitizeOptimizedDependencySourceMap(payload: string) {
    const sourceMap = JSON.parse(payload) as SourceMapWithSourcesContent
    if (!Array.isArray(sourceMap.sourcesContent)) return payload

    const sourcesContent = sourceMap.sourcesContent.map((source) => (typeof source === 'string' ? stripNestedSourceMapDirectives(source) : source))

    return JSON.stringify({ ...sourceMap, sourcesContent })
}

async function respondWithSanitizedDependencyMap(
    server: ViteDevServer,
    requestPath: string,
    response: ServerResponse,
    next: NextFunction,
) {
    try {
        const mapPath = resolveOptimizedDependencyMapPath(server, requestPath)
        const payload = await readFile(mapPath, 'utf8')
        response.setHeader('content-type', JSON_CONTENT_TYPE)
        response.end(sanitizeOptimizedDependencySourceMap(payload))
    } catch (error) {
        next(error instanceof Error ? error : new Error('Failed to sanitize optimized dependency source map'))
    }
}

function handleDependencySourceMapRequest(
    server: ViteDevServer,
    request: IncomingMessage,
    response: ServerResponse,
    next: NextFunction,
) {
    const requestPath = requestPathFromUrl(request.url)
    if (!requestPath || !isOptimizedDependencyMapRequest(requestPath)) {
        next()
        return
    }

    void respondWithSanitizedDependencyMap(server, requestPath, response, next)
}

function dependencySourceMapNoiseFilter(): Plugin {
    return {
        name: 'md2-dependency-source-map-noise-filter',
        apply: 'serve',
        configureServer(server) {
            server.middlewares.use((request, response, next) => handleDependencySourceMapRequest(server, request, response, next))
        },
    }
}

That sentence is an agent’s summary of **`EMFILE: too many open files`**, raised while Vitest/Vite loads dependencies. The recorded failures occur **before tests execute**, repeatedly on MUI icon files.

The strongest suspect is [markdown_source_undo_redo.tsx:2](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/app/src/components/editor/source/markdown_source_undo_redo.tsx:2):

```ts
import { Redo, Undo } from '@mui/icons-material';
```

This imports through the package’s central index, which re-exports **10,750 individual icon modules** in your installed version. Although the component uses only two icons, tooling can traverse the whole index during loading. MUI explicitly [recommends individual icon imports to avoid this overhead](https://mui.com/material-ui/guides/minimizing-bundle-size/).

The relevant numbers are:

- **21 test files** imported by the [actions grouped wrapper](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/app/src/components/actions/actions_no_mock.test.tsx:1).
- **10,750 icon modules**, plus their supporting dependencies, reachable through that icon index.
- **2 test workers** configured for UI tests.
- **Unknown simultaneous open-file count** at failure: the logs don’t measure it. The 10,750 figure is the dependency count, not a measured Windows limit.

“Grouped runner” is therefore a misleading diagnosis: recorded runs also fail with **one test file selected**. Dependency loading appears to be the main pressure.

The component’s latest commit is dated **October 4**, which fits the recent timing, though I haven’t reproduced the failure to prove causality. The likely fix is to import `@mui/icons-material/Redo` and `/Undo` individually, matching the rest of the codebase.

---
id: B_260
internalId: ef3c3a56-28a9-4ca5-9402-16972e140c01
title: Source indentation is lost when returning to Rich text
status: new
after: e461b100-4b8f-435e-9c0f-81426d7fdb47
---

Reported during review of [PR #29](https://github.com/jan-bogaerts/md2/pull/29), head `146ca4bb105c90cab3739d7f6356096608d6dfd8`. Fix after the PR is merged.

## Reproduction

1. Open a Markdown document containing `code` as an ordinary paragraph.
2. Switch to Source and add four leading spaces: `    code`.
3. Switch back to Rich text.
4. Add another paragraph and save.

Rich text still shows an ordinary paragraph instead of an indented code block. The subsequent rich edit exports `code` without its indentation, losing the Source change.

Expected: returning to Rich text imports the indented code block. Later edits, saving, and reopening preserve its code-block meaning; serialization may use a fenced code block.

## Cause and affected code

`MarkdownSourceController.setMode()` detects the Source change using exact comparison, but publishes `viewMode$` to let MDXEditor import it. MDXEditor's `setMarkdown$` compares trimmed strings and skips importing when only outer whitespace differs. Here, the leading whitespace changes Markdown meaning, so the rich document remains stale and its next export overwrites the Source edit.

Affected files: `app/src/components/editor/source/markdown_source_controller.ts` and the shared `markdown_editor.tsx` integration. MDXEditor's comparison is in `@mdxeditor/editor/dist/plugins/core/index.js`.

The fix must import meaningful Source whitespace changes while preserving untouched source, clean-state behavior, and the existing undo baseline rules. Do not treat whitespace-only differences as equivalent without considering Markdown meaning.

## Regression coverage

- Change a paragraph into an indented code block in Source, return to Rich text, and verify code-block rendering.
- Make an unrelated rich edit, save, and reopen; verify the code-block meaning survives.
- Verify viewing Source without editing preserves the original text and rich undo history.

The indentation loss was reproduced with a temporary regression probe against the installed MDXEditor in `markdown_editor_reliability.real.test.tsx`. The probe was removed after review. No fix is included in this report.

id: B_264
internalId: 78b279d6-eae4-4801-92c0-a6423a1fc880
title: Action input rerenders unrelated controls while typing
status: ready for implementation
---

## Problem and evidence

Use **Chrome DevTools attached to Electron’s main process** to record a JavaScript CPU profile. Electron’s built-in window DevTools profiles the renderer. [Electron documentation](https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/tutorial/debugging-main-process)

For this project:

1. Keep your frontend development server running.
2. Open PowerShell at the repository root and run:

   ```powershell
   Set-Location desktop
   Remove-Item Env:ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
   $env:MD2_APP_URL = 'http://localhost:5173'
   .\node_modules\.bin\electron.cmd --inspect=9229 .
   ```

   Launch Electron directly because your `start_electron.js` currently doesn’t forward command-line arguments.

3. Open **`chrome://inspect`** in Chrome. If necessary, click **Configure** and add `localhost:9229`.
4. Click **Inspect** beneath the Electron main-process target.
5. Open **Performance**, click **Record**, reproduce the slow operation in your app, then stop recording. Save the profile using the panel’s export button. [Chrome profiling guide](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/performance/nodejs)

Look at **Bottom-up** for functions consuming the most CPU and **Call tree** for their callers.

For startup profiling, use `--inspect-brk=9229` instead: Electron pauses before executing the main script, allowing you to attach, start recording, then resume.

If you need a timeline covering Chromium threads and multiple processes, use Electron’s [`contentTracing`](https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/api/content-tracing) API. A CPU profile is the best starting point for slow JavaScript in the main process; it won’t directly explain time spent waiting for asynchronous I/O.

Compact new-card and agent prompt editors retain their compact layout and expose Source for conversion recovery. Literal command fields and historical diff views retain their existing behavior. 4- 5-## Start the test checkout 6- -- 22- 23-## Owner checks 24- 25:1. Open a card in list view and in its board popup. Switch between **Rich text** and **Source** without editing; the document must remain clean and its saved source unchanged. Repeat for an instruction and an action's Markdown prompt/phrases. 26:2. Paste the fixture below into Source. Return to Rich text, make an unrelated edit, save, close, and reopen. Both links must resolve, the explicit break must remain a break, and the unused definition must remain in Source. 27:3. Edit one link's destination using its existing dialog. That occurrence may become an inline link; the other reference and its definition must keep their original destination. Copy a reference in Rich text and paste it into another Markdown document; its definition must travel with it. 28:4. In Source, type, undo, redo, paste, and attach/drop a file at a chosen caret position. Confirm these operations affect the visible Source editor. Source undo is local to that Source session. Returning to Rich text after Source edits starts a new rich undo baseline; old content must not return on undo. 29:5. Switch between two cards while in Source. Text and undo must belong to the selected card, and identical reference labels in different cards must retain each card's destination. 30:6. Try `` or `
preserved HTML
`. The editor must recover in Source with the original text intact. Replace it with ordinary Markdown, then return to Rich text. Also check a read-only search preview and a compact new-card or agent prompt editor. Pasting unsupported content into Rich text must preserve the existing document and open Source; paste again there to insert the raw content. 31-7. Check the controls in light and dark themes, plus a literal command field containing backslashes and Markdown punctuation. 32- 33-```markdown 34-# Editing fixture 35- 36:Hard break here\ 37-continues here. 38- 39-Soft newline here -- 45-[unused]: https://unused.example "Keep this definition" 46-``` 47- 48:Rich edits can normalize ordinary Markdown spelling and move definitions to the end of the document while retaining their meaning. Source saves retain the typed text. This PR does not add footnotes, Mermaid, math, or repository-relative image loading. 49- 50-## Automated checks 51- 52-Use the targeted real-editor, editor UI, document binding, draft, and history tests. The editor regressions run against installed MDXEditor/Lexical/CodeMirror rather than the textarea test adapter. **These are used, established packages, and I would keep the direct dependencies while the Source mode feature remains.** They were added in the October 4 change that introduced Source editing and conversion recovery.

| Package | Purpose in this app |
|---|---|
| `@codemirror/commands` | Runs Source editor undo and redo and checks whether those actions are available. |
| `@codemirror/state` | Checks whether Source is read only and creates a text replacement at the selection. |
| `@codemirror/view` | Connects the app’s Source controller to the visible CodeMirror editor for updates, paste handling, and insertion. |
| `mdast-util-from-markdown` | Parses Markdown with the editor’s active syntax extensions so the app can check whether content will import into rich text before switching modes. |

Those uses are in [markdown_source_controller.ts](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/app/src/components/editor/source/markdown_source_controller.ts:1). The feature is wired into the shared [Markdown editor](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/app/src/components/editor/markdown_editor.tsx:482), and its Source behavior has [real editor regression coverage](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/app/src/components/editor/markdown_editor_reliability.real.test.tsx:205).

**Trust:** CodeMirror and `mdast-util-from-markdown` are upstream editor and Markdown ecosystem packages with public documentation and MIT licenses; these do not appear to be obscure substitute libraries. CodeMirror’s [reference manual](https://codemirror.net/docs/ref/) describes the three CodeMirror modules, and the [parser’s repository](https://github.com/syntax-tree/mdast-util-from-markdown) documents its role. The CodeMirror GitHub mirror is archived because its repository [moved to the maintainer’s host](https://github.com/codemirror/commands), rather than being presented as an abandoned package. This is a provenance assessment, not a security audit.

**Complexity:** MDXEditor already depends on all four packages. `npm ls` shows one deduplicated installed version of each, so declaring them directly does not currently add a second copy. Direct declarations are appropriate because this app imports them directly. The substantial added complexity is the custom Source controller and mode transition behavior, not these four dependency entries. That complexity serves documented requirements such as preserving raw Source text, keeping undo tied to the visible editor, and recovering from rich text conversion errors. If those requirements are unwanted, the feature itself is the part to reconsider.
